## Python

```python
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from dgxe import *

wx = pd.read_csv("data/narrabri_weather.csv")
traj = pd.read_csv("data/narrabri_biomass.csv.gz")
drv = make_drivers(wx)
Theta = make_library(drv)
tr = make_trajectories(traj, drv)
```

:::


Every method maps the design matrix $\mathbf{X}$ and the increments $\Delta\mathbf{y}$ of one genotype to a coefficient vector, with the intercept first. A method is therefore a function `fit(X, dy)`, and methods can be exchanged freely. Genotype `g001` is used here.

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

## Methods

Each tab describes one method and shows its code.

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Least squares

Ordinary least squares minimises the residual sum of squares, $\hat{\boldsymbol{\xi}} = \arg\min \lVert \Delta\mathbf{y} - \mathbf{X}\boldsymbol{\xi}\rVert_2^2$. It has no hyperparameter and no term is removed. R: `lm.fit`; Python: `numpy.linalg.lstsq`.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
show_fun("fit_ols", level = 3)
```

## Ridge

Ridge regression adds a squared penalty, $\lVert \Delta\mathbf{y} - \mathbf{X}\boldsymbol{\xi}\rVert_2^2 + \lambda \lVert\boldsymbol{\xi}\rVert_2^2$, which shrinks the coefficients of correlated terms but removes none. The hyperparameter is $\lambda$. R: `glmnet`; Python: closed form, with the penalty scaled as in `glmnet`.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
show_fun("fit_glmnet", "fit_ridge", level = 3)
```

## Lasso

The lasso penalises the absolute values, $\lVert \Delta\mathbf{y} - \mathbf{X}\boldsymbol{\xi}\rVert_2^2 + \lambda \lVert\boldsymbol{\xi}\rVert_1$, and sets coefficients to zero: it selects terms. The hyperparameter is $\lambda$. R: `glmnet`; Python: scikit-learn `ElasticNet` with the penalty scaled as in `glmnet`.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
show_fun("fit_glmnet", "fit_lasso", level = 3)
```

## Elastic net

The elastic net mixes both penalties (here in equal parts) and keeps groups of correlated terms together more readily than the lasso. The hyperparameter is $\lambda$. Implementation as for the lasso.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
show_fun("fit_glmnet", "fit_enet", level = 3)
```

## Best subset

Best-subset selection finds the $k$ terms with the smallest residual sum of squares, $\min \lVert \Delta\mathbf{y} - \mathbf{X}\boldsymbol{\xi}\rVert_2^2$ subject to at most $k$ non-zero coefficients. With $K = 12$ terms all subsets can be searched (R: `leaps`; Python: residual sums of squares from the Gram matrix). The hyperparameter is $k$.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
show_fun("fit_subset", level = 3)
```

## Backward elimination

Backward elimination starts from all terms and repeatedly removes the term whose removal increases the residual sum of squares least, until $k$ terms remain. It is the same function as best subset with `method = "backward"`, and is much cheaper for large libraries. The hyperparameter is $k$.

## STLSQ

Sequential thresholded least squares is the algorithm of the original SINDy method: fit by least squares, remove the terms whose scaled coefficient (coefficient times the standard deviation of the term, relative to that of the increments) is below a threshold, and refit on the remaining terms until no term is removed. The hyperparameter is the threshold.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
show_fun("fit_stlsq", level = 3)
```

:::

Scaled to a common size (coefficient times the standard deviation of the term, relative to that of the increments), the sparsity pattern of each method is visible; empty cells are terms that were removed.

## Python

```python
from matplotlib.colors import LinearSegmentedColormap, TwoSlopeNorm

size = d.X.std(axis=0, ddof=1) / d.dy.std(ddof=1)
effect = fits.iloc[1:].mul(size, axis=0)
colours = LinearSegmentedColormap.from_list("dgxe", [BURGUNDY, "white", BLUE])
colours.set_bad("#F3F4F6")                       # removed terms

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 3.6))
image = ax.imshow(effect.where(effect != 0), cmap=colours,
                  norm=TwoSlopeNorm(0), aspect="auto")
ax.set_xticks(range(effect.shape[1]), effect.columns, rotation=30, ha="right")
ax.set_yticks(range(effect.shape[0]), effect.index)
fig.colorbar(image, label="scaled coefficient")
fig.tight_layout()
```

:::

```{r}
#| label: 04-3-run
#| echo: false
#| fig-height: 3.6
size <- apply(d$X, 2, sd) / sd(d$dy)
effect <- fits[-1, ] * size
long <- data.frame(term = factor(rownames(effect), rev(rownames(effect))),
                   method = factor(rep(colnames(effect), each = nrow(effect)),
                                   colnames(effect)),
                   effect = as.vector(effect))

ggplot(long, aes(method, term, fill = ifelse(effect == 0, NA, effect))) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.6) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = dgxe[["burgundy"]], mid = "white",
                       high = dgxe[["blue"]], na.value = "#F3F4F6") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = "scaled\ncoefficient") +
  theme_dgxe() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1),
        axis.line = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "right")
```

The coefficients of correlated terms are not determined individually (powers of one driver, and thermal time and day length, are strongly correlated), so the selected terms differ between methods. The methods are compared by prediction on unseen seasons in step 5.

## Exploring a method

Each method has one hyperparameter: the threshold of STLSQ, the penalty $\lambda$ of ridge, lasso and elastic net, or the number of terms $k$ of subset selection. The left panel shows the scaled coefficients of the selected genotype for the chosen setting. The right panel shows the held-out trajectory error for all settings of the method, as the mean over the same 20 genotypes. The terms that are retained differ between genotypes, so a change of setting can leave the coefficients of one genotype unchanged and still change the error: select other genotypes to see this.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
d3 = window.d3          // local copies, see js/
Plot = window.Plot
hyper = FileAttachment("data/interactive/hyper.json").json()
viewof method = select("Method", Object.keys(hyper.methods), "STLSQ")
spec = hyper.methods[method]
viewof genotype = select("Genotype", hyper.genotypes, "g001")
viewof step = slider(spec.param, spec.values, Math.floor(spec.values.length / 2), v => (+v).toPrecision(2))
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const all = Object.values(hyper.methods);
  const reach = d3.max(all.flatMap(m => m.effect.flat(2).map(Math.abs)));
  const rmse = [d3.min(all.flatMap(m => m.rmse)), 0.8];   // cap: very large penalties are off scale
  const g = hyper.genotypes.indexOf(genotype);
  const rows = hyper.terms.map((term, i) => ({term, effect: spec.effect[step][g][i]}));
  const curve = spec.values.map((value, i) => ({value, rmse: spec.rmse[i]}));
  const scale = spec.param === "terms" ? "linear" : "log";
  const coefficients = Plot.plot({
    width: 340, height: 300, marginLeft: 50,
    x: {domain: [-reach, reach], label: "scaled coefficient"},
    y: {domain: hyper.terms, label: null},
    marks: [Plot.barX(rows, {x: "effect", y: "term",
              fill: d => d.effect > 0 ? "#014E81" : "#8B1E3F"}),
            Plot.ruleX([0])]
  });
  const error = Plot.plot({
    width: 340, height: 300,
    x: {type: scale, label: spec.param, tickFormat: ".2~g"},
    y: {domain: [rmse[0] - 0.01, rmse[1] + 0.01], label: "held-out RMSE, mean of 20 genotypes (t/ha)"},
    marks: [Plot.line(curve, {x: "value", y: "rmse", stroke: "#9CA3AF", clip: true}),
            Plot.dot(curve, {x: "value", y: "rmse", fill: "#9CA3AF", r: 3, clip: true}),
            Plot.dot([curve[step]], {x: "value", y: "rmse", fill: "#8B1E3F", r: 6, clip: true})]
  });
  return html`<div style="display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:1rem">${coefficients}${error}</div>
    <p class="interactive-note">${genotype}: ${spec.nterms[step][g]} of ${hyper.terms.length} terms retained; mean over the ${hyper.genotypes.length} genotypes: ${d3.mean(spec.nterms[step]).toFixed(1)}.</p>`;
}
```

The figure uses results computed beforehand ([`scripts/precompute_interactive.R`](https://github.com/corne00/dynamic-gxe-workshop/blob/main/scripts/precompute_interactive.R)).
